result.topic_en: Dated diary entries from June–July 1796 on divisors of forms x^2 − a, the theory of polygons and pure equations, a proof by induction, the special case of the congruence x^n − 1 ≡ 0, and a begun statement about integral coefficients when one polynomial is divided by another.
result.transcription:
Demonstrationes elegantiores pro nexu
divisorum formae $\square - a$, $+1$ cum $-1$, $\pm 2$
inveni Jun 17 Gotting
Deductionem secundam theoriae polygonorum
excolui Jul. 17 Gotting
Per utramque methodum monstrari posse
puras tantum aequationes solvi oportere.
Quod Oct. 1. per ind. invenimus demonstratione
munivimus Jul. 20.
Casum singularem solutionis congruentiae $x^n - 1 \equiv 0$
(scilicet quando [-###-] congr. aux: radices aequales habet) qui
tam diu {+nos+} [-me-] vexavit felicissimo successu vicimus, ex
[-...-] congruentiarum solutione si modulus est numeri
primi potestas. [-pot-] Jul. 2[?]
Si $x^{m+n} + ax^{m+n-1} + bx^{m+n-2} \ldots + n$ (A)
per $x^m + \alpha x^{m-1} + \beta x^{m-2} \ldots + m$ (B)
dividatur atque omnes coefficientes in (A) $a, b, c$
&c sint numeri integri
[-nullus numerorum $\alpha, \beta$ ... potest esse numerus ratio-
nalis fractus, si omnes rationales esse-]
